# Connect an AI assistant (MCP setup)

<!-- Generated by `python3 kvm_mcp_setup.py --markdown`; edit kvm_mcp_setup.py instead. -->

`kvm_mcp.py` is a local stdio [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server named `windows-keyboard`. It lets an AI assistant type on the Windows PC through the cable, after you approve each call. See the README for its tools.

The easiest way to get a ready-to-paste config is the app: click **Connect AI Assistant…** (or Help → Connect AI Assistant). It fills in your real paths and has a Copy button. You can also print them from a terminal:

```bash
python3 kvm_mcp_setup.py                   # every assistant
python3 kvm_mcp_setup.py --harness cursor  # just one
```

The examples below use `/Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv` for uv and `/Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard` for this repository. Replace both with absolute paths (`which uv` and `pwd` in your clone). GUI apps don't read your shell `PATH`, so use the full path to `uv`. If a config file already has other servers, add the `windows-keyboard` entry next to them.

> **Safety:** The assistant can't see the Windows screen; it will ask you what happened. Keep tool approval on: don't enable auto-approve, "trust", "always allow" or similar settings for this server, so you review every command before it is typed.

<a id="copilot-app"></a>

## GitHub Copilot app

**Where:** Customize → MCP → add a server, or ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json

Add a local (stdio) server named windows-keyboard with the command and arguments below, or merge this JSON into ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json (shared with Copilot CLI). Restart the app.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "windows-keyboard": {
      "command": "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--directory",
        "/Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard",
        "kvm_mcp.py"
      ],
      "type": "stdio",
      "tools": [
        "*"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Reference: <https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/github-copilot-app/customize-github-copilot-app>

<a id="copilot-cli"></a>

## GitHub Copilot CLI

**Where:** Terminal, or ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json

Run this in a terminal. It writes ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json (the same JSON as the GitHub Copilot app). You can also use /mcp add inside a session. Don't start Copilot with --allow-all-tools for this server.

```bash
copilot mcp add windows-keyboard -- /Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv run --directory /Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard kvm_mcp.py
```

Reference: <https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-mcp-servers>

<a id="vscode"></a>

## VS Code (Copilot Chat)

**Where:** .vscode/mcp.json, or Command Palette → MCP: Open User Configuration

Merge this into .vscode/mcp.json for one workspace, or into the user configuration for all workspaces. Start the server from the MCP view and use it in Agent mode. Keep VS Code's trust and tool confirmation prompts.

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "windows-keyboard": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--directory",
        "/Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard",
        "kvm_mcp.py"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Reference: <https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/mcp-configuration>

<a id="claude-desktop"></a>

## Claude Desktop

**Where:** ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json

Open Settings → Developer → Edit Config, merge this JSON into claude_desktop_config.json, then quit and reopen Claude. Leave tool permissions on "Ask" for this server.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "windows-keyboard": {
      "command": "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--directory",
        "/Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard",
        "kvm_mcp.py"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Reference: <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers>

<a id="claude-code"></a>

## Claude Code

**Where:** Terminal (stored in ~/.claude.json)

Run this in a terminal. --scope user makes the server available in every project. Check it with claude mcp list. Don't add its tools to the allow list or use --dangerously-skip-permissions.

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user windows-keyboard -- /Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv run --directory /Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard kvm_mcp.py
```

Reference: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp>

## Cursor

**Where:** ~/.cursor/mcp.json (or .cursor/mcp.json in a project)

Merge this JSON into ~/.cursor/mcp.json, then check that windows-keyboard is enabled in Cursor Settings → MCP. Keep the default approval mode so the agent asks before each tool call.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "windows-keyboard": {
      "command": "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--directory",
        "/Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard",
        "kvm_mcp.py"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Reference: <https://cursor.com/help/customization/mcp>

<a id="windsurf"></a>

## Windsurf

**Where:** ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json

In Windsurf open Cascade → MCP servers → View raw config (normally ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json), merge this JSON, and refresh the server list. Don't turn on auto-execution for this server.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "windows-keyboard": {
      "command": "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--directory",
        "/Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard",
        "kvm_mcp.py"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Reference: <https://docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/mcp>

<a id="codex"></a>

## OpenAI Codex CLI

**Where:** ~/.codex/config.toml

Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml, or run: codex mcp add windows-keyboard -- /Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv run --directory /Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard kvm_mcp.py. Keep approval_policy at its default ("on-request"); don't set it to "never".

```toml
[mcp_servers.windows-keyboard]
command = "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv"
args = ["run", "--directory", "/Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard", "kvm_mcp.py"]
```

Reference: <https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp>

<a id="gemini"></a>

## Gemini CLI

**Where:** ~/.gemini/settings.json (or .gemini/settings.json in a project)

Merge this into ~/.gemini/settings.json and restart Gemini CLI. Check it with /mcp. Keep "trust": false; true skips every confirmation.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "windows-keyboard": {
      "command": "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--directory",
        "/Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard",
        "kvm_mcp.py"
      ],
      "trust": false
    }
  }
}
```

Reference: <https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/mcp-server/>

<a id="zed"></a>

## Zed

**Where:** ~/.config/zed/settings.json

Merge this into ~/.config/zed/settings.json (or use Settings → AI → MCP Servers → Add Local Server). Keep agent.tool_permissions.default at "confirm".

```json
{
  "context_servers": {
    "windows-keyboard": {
      "command": "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--directory",
        "/Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard",
        "kvm_mcp.py"
      ],
      "env": {}
    }
  }
}
```

Reference: <https://zed.dev/docs/ai/mcp>

## Check it

Ask the assistant to run the `windows_keyboard_status` tool. It types nothing and reports the port, baud rate, whether Windows sees the keyboard, and Caps Lock. From a terminal:

```bash
/Users/YOU/.local/bin/uv run --directory /Users/YOU/src/mac-to-windows-keyboard kvm_mcp.py --status
```
